absent: Exact predicate and configuration conditions for page-granular linear mapping enforcement.
Allocator and split-helper contracts for range conversion and temporary hierarchy construction.
Protection attribute semantics of kernel page protection constants and global versus non-global entries.
Behavior of linear alias validity toggling and read-only enable flag management.
Internals of the external identity-map remap routine and trampoline alias and fixmap layout.
Base-page versus huge-page vmemmap population implementations and node and altmap handling.
Reservation clearing and page instantiation helpers for hotplug add and remove.
Section classification and early-memory determination for offline veto.
Physical to virtual translation and address-width handling for mappable range derivation.
Locking beyond the split mutex for hotplug teardown and empty-table reclamation.

findings.text: Provides a pool readiness check that reports success when the linear map is already page granular or when early initialization already handled the pool, and otherwise requests a split of the pool extent to page granularity under serialization and reports whether that request succeeded without requiring extra invalidation on systems with the stated hardware capability.
Boot-time option handler that interprets an integer argument as a boolean enable for early pool handling and always reports successful parsing.

Establishes a read-only state for kernel read-only sections and initial text by clearing a writable flag once and applying read-only protection to two extents, one covering notes and exception data via the init boundary and one covering the gap between text markers, then revokes validity of the data alias in the linear map.
Selects between read-only-executable and executable protection for kernel text depending on whether read-only data protection is enabled.

Early setup that does nothing when the kernel remains mapped at EL0, and otherwise installs a global executable mapping for trampoline text at its alias in a dedicated top-level table while also establishing fixed mappings for each text page plus an extra read-only fixed mapping when relocation support is present.

Coordinates a multiprocessor transition to non-global mappings where the bootstrap processor prepares zeroed hierarchy storage adjusted for the active level count and builds a temporary addressable window, every processor switches through an identity map to invoke an external remap routine with identity, population, temporary root and window parameters, then the bootstrap processor releases the scratch storage and enables the non-global mode flag, aborting boot if temporary construction fails.
Temporary window address for the non-global install sequence is the arithmetic negation of one shifted by the PMD shift.
Serialization for on-demand splitting of the pool range relies on a dedicated page-table split mutex held only around the split request.

Teardown of a hotplug range walks the kernel hierarchy from top to bottom clearing entries, treating leaves and tables distinctly, freeing backing pages only when requested and otherwise performing a single range-wide invalidation, while per-page or single-page invalidation accompanies freeing of small or large leaves and altmap use without freeing is considered inconsistent.

Reclamation of empty intermediate tables requires the affected range to be aligned and contained within supplied floor and ceiling bounds, verifies that all sibling entries are empty after prior clearing, then clears the parent, invalidates the table entry from the TLB, and frees the table page, with guards that skip levels not enabled by configuration.

Backing and table page release distinguishes altmap-backed extents from ordinary buddy extents, derives buddy order from size, warns on reserved ordinary pages, and runs a table destructor before freeing single table pages.

Population entry validates that the requested extent lies inside the vmemmap window and does not span more than one section worth of descriptors, then delegates to a base-page path for non-4K configurations or small extents and to a huge-page path otherwise.
Release entry validates vmemmap bounds, then unmaps the extent while freeing backing store with altmap support and reclaims newly emptied tables bounded by the vmemmap window.

Large-entry helpers leave the P4D level as a no-op, conditionally clear PUD and PMD leaves reporting whether a clear occurred, and for table entries clear the parent, flush the table entry, and free the child table, with the PUD variant first draining present child PMD entries.

Hotplug add path validates the physical range, selects mapping restrictions that forbid block and contiguous mappings when page-granular mapping is forced and otherwise forbid execution, creates the linear mapping, clears any no-map reservation, instantiates pages, extends the tracked maximum page numbers, and on any failure removes the partial mapping before reporting the error.

Hotplug remove path withdraws pages for the extent and then removes the linear mapping, where the shared removal helper requires the initial top-level directory and containment in the linear window, unmaps without freeing backing, and reclaims empty tables bounded by that window.

Derivation of the physical range suitable for hotplug uses the physical equivalents of the linear window ends based on the actual address width, normalizes a randomized wrap by starting at zero, warns when inverted, and returns an inclusive range covering both ends except the window terminator.

Removability without splitting is determined by testing whether either edge of the physical extent or of its descriptor extent would fall inside a leaf or contiguous run at any hierarchy level, using alignment shortcuts per level and traversal otherwise, failing closed with a diagnostic naming the physical extent when a split would occur.

Offline veto logic ignores actions other than going-offline and offline, walks the target in section strides skipping non-boot sections, rejects going-offline for boot memory and reports already-offlined boot memory as an unexpected condition, and otherwise rejects the request when edge alignment would require a split, accepting otherwise.

Fragments encode defensive checks that warn or abort on reserved frees, absent or malformed hierarchy entries during teardown, contiguous entries in descriptor mappings, misaligned or oversized vmemmap requests, mappings outside expected directories or windows, disallowed offline attempts, and failure to build the temporary install hierarchy.
